title: Credential alias collision enables intermittent cross-org authorization
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (hosted + dedicated + private installs) reported intermittent 403/200 mismatches where requests authenticated with API credentials for Org A occasionally succeeded against Org B resources. Impact: cross-organization elevation risk for a small subset of requests; correlated with high churn of short-lived credential aliases and token refreshes during autoscale bursts. Scope: affects API key alias resolution and token-to-org mapping in the auth proxy used by hosted and Dedicated; in Private installs the misconfiguration surfaced when customers had alias-sync enabled for key migration tools.

Reproduction steps (observed in staging):
1) Create two orgs (org-a, org-b) and two API key aliases that share the same short prefix hash during migration.
2) Rapidly rotate alias A while concurrently issuing token refresh for long-lived session tokens.
3) Send parallel requests (burst) using old token but new alias metadata. Some requests resolve to the wrong org mapping due to race in alias lookup cache invalidation.

Root cause: collision between the credential alias prefix map (an in-memory map keyed by 8-char alias prefix) and our multi-layer cache invalidation. When alias entries are replaced during rotation, a short window exists where the prefix lookup returns a newly inserted entry before the token->org binding has been updated. The token refresh path assumes deterministic alias->org binding; it does not account for alias prefix reuse across different tenants. A contributing factor: aggressive prefix-shortening optimization introduced to reduce index size in runtime-1.21.

Mitigation (short term):
- Hotfix deployed to hosted-auth-proxy to fall back to full-length alias lookup when token org mismatch is detected (rolled out 2026-03-11 + feature-flagged).
- Lifted aggressive alias prefix reuse in Dedicated autoscale images by disabling short-prefix optimization in config for affected clusters.
- Customer-facing mitigation guidance published and pushed to active escalations: recommend immediate key rotation + disable alias-sync for Private until fix is applied.

Planned fix (long term):
1) Replace 8-char prefix index with collision-resistant mapping using (alias-prefix, creation-timestamp, org-id) tuple and persistent metadata versioning.
2) Update token refresh flow to validate alias metadata version and retry transparent lookup on mismatch.
3) Add CI fuzz tests that simulate alias collisions and high-concurrency rotations.
4) Add canary monitors that detect divergence between token->org binding and alias map (alert P0).

Rollout plan:
- Merge PR to auth-proxy (target: 2026-03-14) behind feature flag.
- Canary on 5% of hosted traffic for 24h; promote to 50% then full if no regression.
- Dedicated: ship patch into next maintenance window (coordinated via Release Ops).
- Private: provide installable patch and advisory (customers with alias-sync get priority).

Observability & telemetry changes:
- Emit alias_lookup.version and token_binding.version to traces.
- New metric alias_mismatch_retries.count to track transient mismatches.
- Dashboard widget added to Console for affected orgs and recent rotations.

Related artifacts:
- Support tickets: S-23841, S-23863, S-23890
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Auth+Alias+Collision+Runbook
- GH PR (hotfix): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/482
- GH PR (planned): https://github.com/redwood-inference/auth-proxy/pull/491

Notes: This differs from earlier "rotation race" issues because root cause is intentional prefix-shortening optimization combined with alias reuse across orgs; not a simple refresh race. The hotfix reduces customer impact quickly but a proper schema change is required to eliminate collision class entirely.
